output_list.reason: The 'mintToken' function has an integer overflow attack vulnerability. When 'mintedAmount' is very large, the 'totalSupply' += mintedAmount' operation will cause an overflow and set 'totalSupply' to a negative value, aka 'initialUserBalance' in the user's balance can be set to a very large value during 'initialUserBalance' function call.

The 'transfer' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When 'amount' is very large, the 'balanceOf[msg.sender] -= amount' operation will cause an overflow and not reduce 'msg.sender's balance, aka 'initialUserBalance' in the attacker's balance can be set to a very large value during 'initialUserBalance' function call.

The 'transferFrom' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When 'amount' is very large, the 'balanceOf[msg.from] -= amount' and 'allowance[msg.from][msg.sender] -= amount' operations will cause an overflow and not reduce 'msg.from's balance and 'msg.sender's allowance, aka 'initialUserBalance' in the attacker's balance can be set to a very large value during 'initialUserBalance' function call.
The 'freezeAccount' function has a wrong access control vulnerability. It uses 'throw' to revert state changes, which hides error messages, beneficial to attackers without revealing any information.
The 'setPrices' function has a wrong access control vulnerability. It uses 'throw' to revert state changes, which hides error messages, beneficial to attackers without revealing any information.
